title: Best AI Ticketing Systems for IT Teams in 2026
summary: Compare the 12 best AI ticketing systems for IT teams, including Unthread, ServiceNow, Freshservice, and more for automation, workflows, knowledge, and ITSM.
body_text: IT teams do not usually struggle because they lack a place to store tickets. The harder challenge is turning employee questions into correctly classified work, resolving routine issues quickly, and preserving enough context for access requests, incidents, changes, provisioning, and escalations. As request volume grows, manual triage and scattered follow-up can consume the time specialists need for complex troubleshooting and security-sensitive work. This guide evaluates AI ticketing systems against the work internal IT teams handle every day. The comparison emphasizes identity and access requests, software and device support, incident coordination, change approvals, knowledge-based resolution, endpoint and asset integrations, service performance, and the administrative effort required after implementation. Key Takeaways AI should be tested against real IT workflows, not only ticket summaries or response drafting. Unthread combines collaboration-channel intake with purpose-built AI, knowledge management, SLAs, analytics, and workflow automation. Identity, asset, endpoint, development, alerting, and service-management integrations determine how much work can be completed safely and automatically. Incident, change, escalation, and human-handoff behavior matter as much as self-service deflection. IT teams should measure automatic resolution, reassignment, SLA performance, repeat issues, and time returned to specialists. 1) Unthread: Best for Multi-Department IT Operations Best For IT teams that want AI-assisted ticketing, service workflows, and employee intake across Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, chat, and portals without forcing employees into a separate service desk interface. Unthread's Primary Focus Unthread organizes the daily work of internal IT teams, including access requests, software provisioning, device troubleshooting, onboarding, incidents, service changes, and escalations. Employee conversations become structured tickets with ownership, service targets, knowledge, approvals, and automation attached. Its purpose-built AI agents can answer documented questions, collect missing details, classify and route requests, execute approved actions, and hand work to the right specialist with the original conversation intact. This matters for identity and access workflows, where a request may need manager approval, security checks, application ownership, and an update in a connected system before completion. It also helps with device and software requests by gathering required details early, checking available knowledge, and preserving the employee context if a specialist must take over. Unthread customer examples report automatic resolution of about 40% of incoming tickets across internal teams when documentation and workflows are in place. The figure should be treated as a customer outcome rather than a universal guarantee, but it demonstrates the value of connecting AI with approved knowledge and operational workflows. Key Features Purpose-built AI agents for triage, routing, response assistance, and automatic resolution across multiple Tier 1 workflows. Unified intake across Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, employee portals, and chat. Self-learning knowledge management that identifies documentation gaps and drafts updates from resolved requests. Automation for approvals, provisioning, escalations, follow-up steps, notifications, and connected-system actions. Private workflows for sensitive HR, finance, legal, and security requests. SLA and SLO tracking, analytics, on-call rotations, incident and change management, API access, webhooks, and custom agentic prompts. The platform also includes a self-learning knowledge base , an automation builder , and private ticketing for department-specific and sensitive work. These features help IT teams connect employee intake with resolution steps rather than treating AI as a separate chatbot. Internal Support Fit Unthread is useful for IT organizations that receive requests across several collaboration channels and need one operating model for ownership, prioritization, service targets, and reporting. It can also turn Slack into a Slack-based internal help desk while preserving Microsoft Teams, email, chat, and portal intake in the same workflow. The same platform can support HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations while preserving department-specific routing and privacy. Administrators can update forms, approvals, knowledge, service targets, and automation rules as internal processes change, which helps reduce long-term operating overhead. 2) Zendesk Primary Focus Multi-channel ticket and case management across internal and external service environments. Key Features Ticket management across email, messaging, forms, and other channels. AI assistance and self-service options. Knowledge base, reporting, and analytics. Large service integration ecosystem. Internal Support Fit Zendesk may fit IT teams that already use the platform or want employee and customer workflows in one broader service stack. Internal teams should test private requests, collaboration actions, approval depth, and support for incident, asset, and change workflows. 3) Risotto Primary Focus Slack-focused AI assistance and automation for common internal IT requests. Key Features Slack-based request intake. AI assistance for repeat IT questions. Automation for selected access and software workflows. Knowledge-grounded responses. Internal Support Fit Risotto may fit Slack-centered IT teams with a focused request scope. Teams should compare workflow breadth, administration, reporting, escalation behavior, and support beyond access-related work. 4) ServiceNow Primary Focus Enterprise ITSM and service management for formal, governed operating models. Key Features Incident, problem, change, and request management. Enterprise service management capabilities. AI and automation across service workflows. Large integration and partner ecosystem. Internal Support Fit ServiceNow may fit enterprises with formal ITIL practices, dedicated administration, and complex governance. IT leaders should evaluate deployment scope, ongoing configuration ownership, collaboration-channel experience, and the resources needed to maintain the platform. 5) Freshservice Primary Focus Cloud ITSM with service requests, assets, changes, and workflow automation. Key Features Incident and service request management. Asset and change management options. AI assistance through Freshworks capabilities. Workflow automation and approval routing. Internal Support Fit Freshservice may fit IT teams formalizing service desk processes and asset-related workflows. Teams should verify plan-specific AI, collaboration integrations, approval behavior, reporting, and the effort required for ongoing workflow changes. 6) Jira Service Management Primary Focus Service management for Atlassian-centered IT and DevOps teams. Key Features Service request and incident management. Connections with Jira Software and Confluence. Automation and AI capabilities by plan. Knowledge support through Confluence. Internal Support Fit Jira Service Management may fit technical teams already organizing development and operations work in Atlassian products. Buyers should assess employee intake, incident coordination, change workflows, private requests, and the configuration needed for nontechnical departments. 7) InvGate Service Management Primary Focus ITSM workflows connected with asset-management practices. Key Features Request, incident, change, knowledge, and SLA workflows. Connections to IT asset management. Automation, reporting, and self-service. Structured ticket lifecycle management. Internal Support Fit InvGate may fit IT teams seeking formal service processes with asset context. Buyers should confirm collaboration actions, implementation scope, reporting depth, and support for employee requests that extend beyond the IT department. 8) Rezolve.ai Primary Focus Microsoft Teams-centered conversational automation for internal IT. Key Features Teams-based employee interactions. AI assistance for common requests. Workflow automation for internal IT tasks. Knowledge retrieval and self-service. Internal Support Fit Rezolve.ai may fit Microsoft 365 organizations prioritizing Teams-based self-service. Teams should test workflow depth, knowledge requirements, administrative controls, escalation paths, and multi-department privacy. 9) Moveworks Primary Focus Enterprise conversational AI across internal systems and service platforms. Key Features Conversational AI for employee requests. Enterprise integrations across internal systems. Routing and workflow automation. Support for IT and broader employee-service use cases. Internal Support Fit Moveworks may fit large enterprises with established service platforms and implementation resources. Teams should evaluate governance, rollout scope, administration, integration ownership, and fit with their current ITSM environment. 10) Aisera Primary Focus AI service automation across IT, HR, and other service domains. Key Features AI agents for service workflows. Knowledge retrieval and self-service. Automation across internal systems. Service reporting and analytics. Internal Support Fit Aisera may fit organizations evaluating broader AI service automation. Teams should confirm available workflows, confidence controls, governance, implementation requirements, and how easily administrators can maintain knowledge and automation over time. 11) SysAid Primary Focus ITSM workflows for requests, incidents, problems, changes, and assets. Key Features Incident and request management. Problem and change management. Asset management capabilities. AI and automation options for IT workflows. Internal Support Fit SysAid may fit IT departments needing broad ITSM functions. Teams should evaluate intake, collaboration integrations, configuration, reporting, and the employee experience for both routine and sensitive requests. 12) Syncro Primary Focus Ticketing connected with endpoint monitoring and management. Key Features Ticketing linked to device management. Automation for IT operations. Remote monitoring and management. AI assistance options for ticket workflows. Internal Support Fit Syncro may fit endpoint-heavy environments or managed service models. Internal IT teams should evaluate whether the RMM-centered operating model matches employee intake, internal-service reporting, and multi-department requirements. How IT Teams Should Evaluate an AI Ticketing System Match AI Capabilities to Common IT Requests Build a test set using password resets, software access, device troubleshooting, onboarding, service incidents, and change requests. Review whether the system answers correctly, gathers required details, applies the right classification, routes work to the correct owner, and completes only approved actions. Test confidence thresholds and human handoff so uncertain requests do not become silent errors. Review Identity, Asset, and Endpoint Workflows AI creates more operational value when it can safely connect tickets with identity providers, device platforms, software systems, asset records, and project tools. Evaluate whether the platform can verify requester context, collect approvals, update connected systems, and record the result in the ticket. For device and endpoint work, confirm whether asset details, ownership, warranty, and security context are available to the specialist. Evaluate Incident, Change, and Escalation Workflows Confirm how urgent issues are prioritized, how on-call teams are engaged, how approvals are captured, and how context moves from AI assistance to human specialists. Review whether incident communications, ownership changes, and timeline updates remain visible. For change workflows, test risk review, approval paths, implementation steps, and rollback documentation rather than assuming ordinary ticket automation covers change control. Measure Resolution Quality and IT Service Performance Track first response, resolution time, automatic resolution, reassignment, SLA compliance, repeat tickets, reopen rates, and escalation outcomes by request category. Separate ticket deflection from automatic resolution so teams know whether the system merely presented information or actually completed the request. Review the time returned to specialists and whether automation reduces manual work without creating more corrections. Compare Administration After Launch Implementation speed is only one part of the decision. IT processes change as tools, approvers, departments, security requirements, and service targets evolve. Confirm how easily administrators can update routing, forms, permissions, knowledge sources, approval steps, integrations, and automation rules without engineering support or repeated professional-services work. Connecting AI Ticketing to Daily IT Operations With Unthread Unthread gives IT teams one internal help desk for employee requests from Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, chat, and portals. Conversations become structured tickets with ownership, priority, routing, SLAs, approvals, and complete context, allowing employees to request help without learning a separate service-desk interface. Its purpose-built AI agents can answer documented questions, collect missing details, classify and route requests, trigger approved workflows, and escalate work with the original conversation attached. IT teams can use these capabilities for access requests, onboarding, software provisioning, password resets, device support, incidents, service changes, and other repeatable Tier 1 work. Unthread also connects knowledge management, analytics, on-call rotations, incident and change management, integrations, API access, and automation in one operating model. This allows specialists to focus on complex troubleshooting, security-sensitive tasks, and changes requiring judgment while administrators continue adjusting routing, approvals, documentation, and service targets as IT processes evolve. Frequently Asked Questions What should IT teams test during an AI ticketing pilot? Use real examples from access, software, devices, onboarding, incidents, changes, and recurring questions. Measure answer accuracy, successful completion, routing quality, escalation behavior, reassignment, SLA performance, and the administrative effort needed to correct workflows or knowledge. Include both routine and ambiguous requests so the team can see how confidence controls and human handoff work. Is ticket deflection the same as automatic resolution? No. Deflection provides information that may prevent a ticket or reduce specialist effort, while automatic resolution completes the request or confirms a supported outcome. For example, showing a password-reset article is deflection. Verifying the requester, triggering an approved reset workflow, confirming completion, and closing the ticket is automatic resolution. IT teams should measure these outcomes separately. Which integrations matter most for IT teams? Identity, endpoint, asset, software, project, documentation, alerting, and collaboration integrations usually have the greatest operational impact. Their value depends on what the workflow can do, not merely whether an integration exists. Teams should test whether the system can read the right context, perform approved updates, preserve audit history, and return a clear result to the employee and specialist. How should sensitive or privileged IT requests be handled? Use role-based access, restricted workflows, audit trails, approval controls, and clear escalation paths for security-sensitive or privileged work. Requests involving administrator access, security incidents, confidential investigations, or regulated systems should expose only the information required by each participant. AI should not execute privileged actions without explicit controls, validation, and a documented record. When is Unthread a strong fit for IT? Unthread is a strong fit when employees request help through Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, chat, or portals and IT wants ticketing, AI, knowledge, service levels, automation, and analytics in one operating model. It is especially relevant when IT needs to automate repeatable Tier 1 work, preserve conversation context, support private requests, and later extend the same structured approach to HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations.

title: AI for Good: Matching great potential with great responsibility
summary: We have real opportunities that can unite us toward a common goal of making AI a positive force for people's lives and work. AI is here to stay, and it is up to us to intentionally envision and shape a positive future. Let us start by understanding AI, asking the right questions, having a human-centric vision for using the technology, and collaborating with an ecosystem of players.
body_text: As the Global Head of AI Enablement, my daily conversations center around using artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly to deliver trusted outcomes for CGI and our clients. But I don't need to be an AI executive to experience its vast reach. My children use AI tools to help them gather sources for their university research assignments, and my mother used AI tools to plan her hotel layover in Paris. The pace of AI's advancement has already overtaken previous disruptive technologies like the Internet and mobile devices. According to our 2024 CGI Voice of Our Clients research, AI is a top business, IT and innovation priority. Across industries, CGI’s research reveals that 26% of executives interviewed are implementing traditional AI—up 10 percentage points year-over-year—and 79% are investigating or conducting proofs of concept for generative AI. This is no surprise given AI’s potential to accelerate optimization and growth. While the AI opportunities vs. risks debate continues, organizations that understand AI's potential also acknowledge the responsibility that comes with its use. This means focusing on ways to responsibly integrate AI into the multifaceted dimensions of our daily lives. Accelerating positive outcomes for society We see many examples where AI is helping solve some of the world's biggest challenges. Here are a few: Improving quality of life : translating the brain activity of a paralyzed woman into words and accelerating the identification and accuracy of measuring sleep apnea . Addressing climate change : building digital twins of our planet to drive sustainable practices and improving climate policy. Combating pollution : using AI to predict pollution before it happens and help prevent it. Accelerating the energy transition : making solar panels more efficient and turning CO2 into useful fuels by autonomously testing materials at high computing powers. Advancing scientific discovery : saving researchers hundreds of millions of years and trillions of dollars and accelerating progress on breaking down single-use plastics and finding new malaria vaccines.1 Creating a more equitable world There is growing interest in using AI to advance diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I)—a topic close to my heart. I am passionate about advancing DE&I progress both at CGI and in my community. I coach women within and outside CGI, including the Canadian high school international women's business team. AI's potential in the DE&I realm includes: Reducing unconscious bias in recruitment by using AI-powered tools to shortlist candidates based on experience and skills, rather than demographic factors such as age, ethnicity or gender. Managing origin- and gender-based differences in treatment and diagnoses in healthcare . Reducing human bias and racial prejudice in law enforcement and justice . Analyzing media content and literature to create more equitable representation, flag misinformation, and personalize content. Improving accessibility through assistive technologies and inclusive design. The great responsibility starts with... 1. Understanding AI and questioning how it works To make a positive difference with AI, or for that matter, any technology, understanding how it works is the first step. There are three important parts to AI: the design of the algorithms, the data on which the technology is trained, and the decision-making processes included in the models. For example, if we look at gender diversity: We can start by understanding the design step. A study by UNESCO reveals that women occupy only 20% of technical roles in major machine learning companies, while only 12% of AI researchers globally are female. However, according to the World Economic Forum's Global Gender Gap Report 2024 , the concentration of female talent in AI engineering has more than doubled since 2016, signaling a positive sign of improvement in gender parity. This is just one example. Overall, there needs to be more diverse representation throughout the AI development life cycle. With generative AI's potential to enable customized learning, AI can be a positive force in further improving this curve. Underlying training data also often has an inherent bias. For example, training data for a recruitment algorithm that overrepresents males or specific demographics may hinder diverse hiring. AI can also be used to increase racial diversity in hiring. There is currently a lot of work underway to improve AI models to reduce racial biases. For example, Google Research Center is releasing the Monk Skin Tone (MST) scale for Computer Vision systems to understand human skin tones better and help the broader industry reduce biases. Finally, human decision-making, or human-in-the-loop machine decision-making, must be based on trusted data or an awareness of underlying biases. My colleague Diane Gutiw shares how we closely monitored a chatbot in the healthcare space to ensure it yielded accurate and in-context results. 2. Having a positive human-centric vision Human-centric design is another area where AI offers immense potential. It is about enabling the intrinsic ability of humans, not taking away from it. For example, AI speech translations, text-to-voice and vice versa can improve accessibility and break down communication barriers tremendously. Generative AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, or Microsoft's Copilot for Microsoft365 are already improving productivity and creativity, making work more motivating, fun and enjoyable for many individuals. Developing a human-centric positive vision is essential to ensuring positive outcomes. My colleague Fred Miskawi outlines what this could look like in his blog on human + artificial intelligence . 3. Building an ecosystem of trusted partners To realize the potential of AI, working alone is not an option. Organizations need trusted partners, lawmakers and governments to operate in sync. Think about partners that deeply understand the technology and the evolving regulatory scene and ones that have a vast, trusted ecosystem of partners of their own. For example, local and international consortiums of government officials, regulators, leaders and scientists from research institutes and large technology firms can facilitate the ethical and responsible use of AI. Where do we go from here? We have real opportunities that can unite us toward a common goal of making AI a positive force for people's lives and work. AI is here to stay, and it is up to us to intentionally envision and shape a positive future. Let us start by understanding AI, asking the right questions, having a human-centric vision for using the technology, and collaborating with an ecosystem of players. Contact me if you'd like to discuss more.

AI-powered RFP response software can compress that timeline to days or hours, but only when it’s built especially for government contracting, where FAR rules, Section L/M alignment, and CUI handling define success or failure. We reviewed the leading AI proposal writing tools to identify which ones truly support federal proposal workflows because the gap between generic AI and GovCon-ready software shows up quickly when teams try to pursue more bids without increasing headcount. TLDR: AI proposal tools cut government contractor response time from weeks to hours with automated compliance matrices and requirement tracking. Native Microsoft Word integration preserves your existing workflows while adding AI capabilities. Federal-focused proposal automation providers support the full proposal lifecycle from bid/no-bid decisions through final compliance review using citation-backed AI. Purpose-built tools scale proposal output without increasing headcount or sacrificing compliance. What Are AI Proposal Writing Tools for Government Contractors? AI proposal writing tools for government contractors are software solutions built to automate responses to federal, state, and local government solicitations. These tools apply AI to handle tasks that normally take weeks: analyzing RFP requirements, generating compliant content, and tracking Section L instructions against Section M evaluation criteria. These solutions differ from general writing assistants because they're built for the compliance requirements of government contracting. They parse FAR-informed solicitations, map requirements to responses, and verify that every solicitation element is covered. The result is faster proposal production without quality tradeoffs. Your team can respond to more opportunities while maintaining the accuracy government evaluators expect. FAQs About AI Proposal Writing Tools for Government Contractors Can AI proposal tools actually maintain compliance with complex government requirements? Yes, purpose-built tools automate compliance through features like requirement shredding, automated compliance matrices, and Section L/M tracking. Look for solutions that provide citation-backed content generation and real-time compliance checking to verify every RFP requirement is covered before submission. What's the typical time savings when implementing an AI proposal writing tool? Most contractors report reducing proposal creation from weeks to hours or days. Some contractors report responding to 3-4x more opportunities with the same resources, with some solutions claiming first drafts in 60 minutes versus 60 hours for manual processes. Should I focus on a specialized proposal tool or an all-in-one opportunity management tool? Specialized proposal tools provide deeper functionality for compliance automation, color team reviews, and amendment tracking. All-in-one tools combining opportunity discovery with proposal development work well for smaller teams, but may lack advanced proposal-specific features that larger contractors need to win complex bids. The most capable solutions automate the compliance-heavy steps that traditionally consumed the most time, including shredding RFPs, mapping Section L instructions to Section M evaluation criteria, and tracking solicitation amendments, instead of simply providing a general-purpose writing assistant. What AI tools can help a small government contracting firm write more RFP responses? Small government contracting firms face a specific challenge: limited BD staff and proposal resources mean that every additional RFP response requires either overtime or a hard trade-off against other pursuits. AI proposal tools tackle this by compressing the most labor-intensive steps, including compliance matrix creation, requirement shredding, and first-draft generation, from days to hours. GovEagle is designed to scale proposal output without proportionally increasing headcount, allowing small teams to pursue considerably more opportunities per quarter using the same resources. Native Microsoft Word integration means proposal managers work in familiar tools instead of learning a new tool, reducing the adoption burden that often stalls software investments at smaller firms. For small contractors, the key evaluation criterion is how quickly the tool reduces per-proposal hours on compliance work, not how many features it includes. What AI proposal tools are FedRAMP compliant and safe for handling sensitive government contract data? FedRAMP compliance is a meaningful baseline for any AI proposal tool that handles CUI or sensitive government contract data, but the appropriate authorization level depends on the contractor's work. GovEagle operates at FedRAMP Moderate equivalency with NIST 800-171 compliance, which meets the security baseline for most civilian agency contracts and many defense programs. GovSignals holds FedRAMP High authorization, making it one of the few AI proposal tools suitable for contractors regularly handling the most sensitive unclassified DoD data. Awarded AI has achieved FedRAMP Moderate Authorization and SOC 2 Type 2 certification. Contractors pursuing CMMC compliance or working on programs with specific CUI handling requirements should verify that any solution's authorization level and data handling architecture align with their contractual obligations before onboarding proposal content. Talk to GovEagle's team about security. How does AI proposal automation actually work for government contractors and what results can I expect? AI proposal automation for government contractors works by ingesting the solicitation document (typically an RFP, RFQ, or sources-sought) and applying trained models to extract requirements, map them to evaluation criteria, and generate compliant draft content grounded in the contractor's past proposals and writing style. GovEagle's workflow, for example, shreds the RFP in minutes to produce an automated compliance matrix in Excel aligned to Section L/M structure, then generates AI-assisted first drafts with citations so proposal managers can verify every claim traces back to a source. On results: most contractors report compressing proposal creation from weeks to hours or days, with some teams going from a 60-hour manual drafting process to a compliant first draft in roughly 60 minutes. Precise Software, a GovEagle customer, cut SME time on early-stage proposals by 80%. The practical outcome is that teams can respond to more opportunities per quarter with the same headcount while maintaining the compliance accuracy that government evaluators expect. Which AI proposal writing tools are best for federal contractors? The best AI proposal writing tools for federal contractors are the ones built around federal procurement mechanics (FAR compliance, Section L/M alignment, amendment tracking, and CUI handling) instead of adapted from generic business-writing or commercial RFP software. GovEagle ranks as the strongest option for mid-sized to large federal contractors submitting multiple proposals per quarter: it covers the full Shipley-aligned lifecycle, generates Excel-native compliance matrices, supports color team reviews, integrates natively with Microsoft Word and SharePoint, and operates in a security environment meeting FedRAMP Moderate equivalency and NIST 800-171. Defense contractors handling high-sensitivity DoD data may also consider GovSignals for its FedRAMP High authorization. For federal contractors who need to increase proposal velocity without adding headcount, the decisive criteria are compliance matrix depth, amendment tracking, and whether the tool integrates into the Microsoft Office workflows your proposal team already uses. Final thoughts on selecting proposal automation tools for government contractors Selecting the right AI proposal writing tool comes down to how well it fits real government contracting work. Teams need tools that interpret FAR-driven solicitations correctly, track every compliance requirement automatically, and work inside the systems they already rely on, especially Microsoft Word. Defense-focused contractors may need FedRAMP High environments, while most civilian and mixed-agency teams gain more flexibility from FedRAMP Moderate-equivalent solutions with tighter drafting and review workflows. GovEagle was built around these realities, combining compliance-first AI, citation-backed drafting, and native Microsoft integration to help government contractors respond faster, reduce risk, and pursue more opportunities without expanding headcount. title: Safety Insurance Group, Inc. Announces Intent to Acquire Northeast Metrowest Insurance Agency
summary: Safety Insurance is a premier provider of auto, home, and business owners insurance in Massachusetts, Maine, and New Hampshire.
body_text: Boston, Massachusetts, October 6, 2022 . Safety Insurance Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:SAFT) (“Safety” or “the Company”) today announced the execution of a non-binding Letter of Intent to acquire, through a wholly-owned subsidiary, the assets and operations of Northeast Insurance Agency, Inc (“Northeast / Metrowest”). The transaction will be subject to customary conditions and is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2022. George M. Murphy, President and Chief Executive Officer, commented: “Safety is proud of our history as an independent agency company and remains committed to the agency channel. Our success is rooted in providing products and services to our agency partners and their policyholders, thereby gaining and holding their respect and loyalty. This acquisition is an exciting opportunity to strengthen our position within the independent agency channel while positioning us for future prosperity. Over 30% of our current policies are handled in our Service Center and there will be numerous synergies that can be recognized by both Safety and Northeast / Metrowest, that will enhance our policyholder services.” Since 1989, Northeast / Metrowest has provided personal and commercial insurance to properly protect its customers by determining the best coverage to suit their unique needs. Over that time, Northeast / Metrowest has grown to include over $40 million in policy premiums and continues to expand its offerings to its customers. Scott Bulger, co-principal of Northeast / Metrowest stated, “We are excited to further our long-term valued partnership with Safety while continuing to provide the products and service we are known for in the New England market.” “We are always looking for ways to grow shareholder value, and the opportunity to acquire an agency with the scale and experience of Northeast / Metrowest provides us an additional revenue platform”, commented David F. Brussard, Safety’s Chairman of the Board of Directors. “Safety and Northeast / Metrowest have had a great partnership for over 20 years and this transaction demonstrates our continued support of the independent agency system. The Safety Board of Directors is committed to providing long-term value and investment return by identifying new opportunities, while continuing to focus on our strong underwriting results and core business.” Following the acquisition, Northeast / Metrowest will continue as a stand-alone business operation within Safety’s holding company under the executive leadership of Mr. Bulger. Upon completion of the transaction, the employees of Northeast / Metrowest will become employees of the Safety subsidiary, providing additional high-quality talent to the Company. Northeast / Metrowest’s offices in Auburn, Falmouth, Needham and Westborough, will continue to operate from their current locations. About Safety Safety Insurance Group, Inc., based in Boston, MA, is the parent of Safety Insurance Company, Safety Indemnity Insurance Company, Safety Property and Casualty Insurance Company, and Safety Northeast Insurance Company. Operating exclusively in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Maine, Safety is a leading writer of property and casualty insurance products, including private passenger automobile, commercial automobile, homeowners, dwelling fire, umbrella and business owner policies. title: e& Drives AI Transformation for Global Workforce with Oracle | Oracle Middle East Regional
body_text: Press Release e& Drives AI Transformation for Global Workforce with Oracle Global technology group leverages embedded AI to modernise experience for its 10,000-strong workforce To address data sovereignty requirements, e& accesses Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications through its OCI Dedicated Region Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates—February 12, 2026 Global technology group e& , is using Oracle Fusion Cloud Human Capital Management (HCM) to prepare its global workforce for the AI economy with embedded artificial intelligence (AI) , generative AI , and AI agents . Marking a first for the UAE, e& is deploying these capabilities on its Oracle CIoud Infrastructure (OCI) Dedicated Region to address national data-sovereignty requirements. e& serves customers across 38 countries in the Middle East, Asia, Africa, and Europe. It offers a portfolio of digital services ranging from advanced connectivity, entertainment, streaming, and financial services to AI-powered solutions, cloud computing, ICT, cybersecurity, and IoT platforms. As e& accelerates its AI-led innovation to deliver new solutions to customers, the organisation sought to equip its 10,000-strong workforce with Oracle Cloud HCM. Marwan Bin Shakar, Chief Technology Officer at e& UAE, said: “Modernising the employee experience is a strategic priority. Oracle Cloud HCM enables us to embed AI across our people processes, enhancing talent development and delivering more personalised employee experiences on a secure, locally deployed OCI Dedicated Region.” “With Oracle Cloud HCM, e& has been able to standardise HR processes across geographies, improve workforce visibility, and equip employees and managers with AI-driven insights to support smarter talent decisions. The new HR platform has helped to automate routine tasks such as interview scheduling, candidate screening, and follow-up communications to accelerate time-to-hire and reduce recruitment costs. Furthermore, with the help of advanced AI algorithms, e& has improved the quality of hiring by matching candidates to roles based on skills, experience, and predicted fit,” said Ali Al Mansoori, Group Chief People Officer at e&. title: Why CBAM Is Straining the Relationship Between Producers and Importers
summary: CBAM is straining producer-importer relationships. Learn why carbon data needs shared infrastructure and how CarbonChain Connect provides it.
body_text: When the EU introduced the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), the policy intent was straightforward: ensure that imported goods face a carbon cost equivalent to that paid by EU producers under the Emissions Trading System, and in doing so reduce the risk of carbon leakage while encouraging lower-emissions production globally. What has proven far more complex is not the principle of CBAM, but the way it is being implemented across real supply chains, where producers and importers are being asked to coordinate on carbon data in ways they never previously had to. CBAM is often described as a reporting obligation, but in practice it has become a test of how well producers and importers can work together under pressure, with incomplete systems, unclear ownership of data, and growing financial consequences attached to getting it wrong. A shared obligation built on unequal footing Under CBAM, importers are legally responsible for submitting emissions data for the goods they bring into the EU, but that data must be generated by producers, calculated at installation level, and aligned with EU-defined methodologies that many non-EU installations have never had to follow before. From the importer’s perspective, this creates an immediate dependency on suppliers for information that is both time-sensitive and commercially material, while still leaving the importer exposed if that information is late, incomplete, or ultimately unverifiable. From the producer’s perspective, CBAM introduces a new category of customer demand that is operationally complex, methodologically unfamiliar, and often poorly coordinated, with multiple buyers requesting similar data in different formats and on different timelines, sometimes with little clarity on how that data will be used or protected once shared. Neither side is failing in its role, but both are operating within a structure that assumes a level of coordination and standardisation that does not exist yet. A different way to approach the problem: enter CarbonChain Connect Sign up to CarbonChain Connect Adam Hearne, CEO & Co-Founder sees this as an opportunity to create the most effective product yet that helps both sides of the trade. “We’re creating the backbone for carbon emissions data. A shared infrastructure where producers and importers meet, share data reliably, and scale with commercial relationship with confidence.” CarbonChain Connect is a consolidation of our end-to-end CBAM compliance capabilities. We offer a suite of three modules, that empower importers and producers to manage CBAM compliance under one, comprehensive platform. When you sign-up to CarbonChain Connect, you get access to three modules - 1. Supplier Catalogue Module: This is CarbonChain’s shared infrastructure for installation-level CBAM data. It lets installation operators and buyers manage, validate, and exchange supplier emissions data in one place, replacing manual outreach with a central workflow. Explore Supplier Catalogue Module 2. Data Sharing Module: Built for companies operating in commodity supply chains, this is the control centre for exchanging CBAM datasets with the companies they buy from (upstream) and sell to (downstream). It’s built to help increase data request volume and acceptance by making requests clearer, follow-ups easier, and access rules transparent — without losing control of sensitive information. Explore Data Sharing Module And, the newly launched, 3. Installations Module: Built for producers responding to CBAM data requests from multiple EU customers, the Installations module lets you prepare your CBAM dataset once and share it securely with everyone - through a guided, verification-ready workflow that reduces errors and rework. For importers, it gives a consistent, structured way to access the data they need with less friction and greater confidence ultimately creating trust that is needed to take them through to verification over a five-year period. Explore the Installations Module We now know that the underlying issue CBAM exposes is not a lack of emissions expertise, but the lack of a shared system that allows producers to generate CBAM-ready data once, manage it over time, and share it consistently with multiple customers, while allowing importers to request, receive, and rely on that data without constant manual intervention. The importer reality: accountability without control For importers, CBAM responsibility sits awkwardly between sustainability, procurement, compliance, and finance, all of which depend on emissions data they do not produce themselves. Many importers find themselves chasing dozens or hundreds of suppliers for information that arrives in spreadsheets, PDFs, or bespoke templates, each requiring interpretation, manual checks, and follow-up questions before it can be used with confidence. As CBAM moves closer to financial liability, this challenge intensifies, because missing or low-quality data no longer just affects reporting accuracy, but directly translates into default values, higher costs, and uncertainty in forecasting and contracting. Importers are expected to manage this risk, but without shared systems they are often left assembling a patchwork of supplier responses that is fragile by design. As Nick Ogilvie, Product Manager and CBAM Lead at CarbonChain, puts it: “CBAM only becomes manageable when emissions data stops being treated as a one-off reporting output and starts being treated as shared infrastructure between producers and importers.” The producer reality: repeated requests and rising pressure Producers, particularly those supplying multiple EU customers, often experience CBAM as a steady accumulation of overlapping demands rather than a single regulatory exercise. Beyond the requests, we are seeing that both producers aren’t necessarily always aware on what’s needed operationally to report the correct data for and importers not always asking for the correct information in the fist place. Installation-level data is often prepared uniquely to answer different customer requests, often under tight deadlines and with limited internal guidance and in some cases in misalignment to the EU CBAM’s reporting methodology, emissions and benchmarks calculation requirements, and verification expectations. At the same time, producers are acutely aware that the quality and timeliness of their CBAM data can influence customer relationships, commercial competitiveness, and even access to the EU market, which raises the stakes of getting it wrong, while offering limited support on how to get it right efficiently. For many producers, the frustration is not the requirement to provide data, but the absence of a clear, reusable way to do so with the confidence to communicate authoritative figures and satisfying every customer interaction. Where the relationship starts to strain The tension between producers and importers does not come from unwillingness on either side, but from the fact that CBAM has effectively turned emissions data into a shared operational dependency without providing shared infrastructure to manage it. Importers push harder as deadlines and costs approach, while producers struggle to respond at scale using tools and processes that were never designed for this level of repetition or scrutiny. Over time, these dynamics risk eroding trust, as importers question data quality and producers feel exposed by ad-hoc data sharing, even when both are acting in good faith. What this means at scale and commercially At scale, the absence of shared infrastructure turns CBAM into a bottleneck, where manual coordination breaks down, procurement decisions are influenced by data availability rather than true emissions performance, and both sides absorb growing operational cost simply to stand still. We’re seeing a rise in individuals offering CBAM consultancy and hedging strategies but while valuable, it does not solve the fundamental problem of CBAM data infrastructure. Commercially, this matters because CBAM is no longer an abstract compliance exercise, but a factor in pricing, supplier selection, contract negotiations, and margin management, meaning that inefficient data exchange increasingly shows up in real financial outcomes. From strained relationships to shared systems The European Commission’s CBAM introduced a shared regulatory obligation — but no shared system to manage it. CarbonChain Connect provides that infrastructure, allowing producers and importers to implement EU requirements reliably and at scale. As the UK develops its own CBAM framework, the need for durable carbon data infrastructure will only accelerate. CBAM is changing the relationship between producers and importers whether they are ready or not, because it requires ongoing collaboration on carbon data that sits at the intersection of compliance, operations, and commercial decision-making. The strain many companies feel today is not a sign that CBAM is unworkable, but a signal that the underlying systems have not yet caught up with the role emissions data is now expected to play. Those who invest early in shared infrastructure will not only find CBAM easier to manage but will also be better positioned as carbon data becomes a permanent feature of global commodity trade, rather than a temporary regulatory hurdle. Explore CarbonChain Connect

title: Quoin Pharmaceuticals Receives FDA IND Clearance to Initiate Phase 2 Study of QRX003 in Peeling Skin Syndrome
summary: Quoin Expects to Initiate Phase 2 Study in 2H 2026, Study Plans to Enroll 6-8 Pediatric and Adult Patients in the U.S. and Europe FDA Expressed No Safety Concerns Over Study Design and Duration of Dosing First-Ever Formal Clinical Study for a Potential Peeling Skin Syndrome Therapy Second Cleared
body_text: News Release Company Overview News & Events News Releases Events & Presentations Stock Information Stock Quote & Chart Historic Price Lookup Investment Calculator Analyst Coverage CVR Holders Financial Information SEC Filings Annual Report and Proxy Statement Special Meetings Corporate Governance Governance Overview Board of Directors Executive Officers Committee Composition Board Diversity Matrix IR Resources Email Alerts Contact IR Quoin Pharmaceuticals Receives FDA IND Clearance to Initiate Phase 2 Study of QRX003 in Peeling Skin Syndrome PDF Version Quoin Expects to Initiate Phase 2 Study in 2H 2026, Study Plans to Enroll 6-8 Pediatric and Adult Patients in the U.S. and Europe FDA Expressed No Safety Concerns Over Study Design and Duration of Dosing First-Ever Formal Clinical Study for a Potential Peeling Skin Syndrome Therapy Second Cleared IND Indication for QRX003, in Addition to Netherton Syndrome Peeling Skin Syndrome Currently Has No Approved Treatment Quoin Anticipates Also Testing QRX003 in Additional Ichthyosis Indications for Which There Are No Approved Treatments ASHBURN, Va., July 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Quoin Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (NASDAQ: QNRX), a late clinical-stage specialty pharmaceutical company focused on rare and orphan diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the Company's Investigational New Drug (IND) application for QRX003 for the treatment of Peeling Skin Syndrome (PSS), enabling initiation of its planned Phase 2 clinical study. Quoin expects to initiate the study in the second half of 2026. Potential clinical sites, clinical investigators and study participants have already been identified. Key Facts Clearance enables Quoin to initiate a Phase 2 clinical study of QRX003 in Peeling Skin Syndrome in the second half of 2026. The study is expected to enroll 6-8 pediatric and adult patients in the United States and Europe. The IND is the first ever submitted to the FDA for Peeling Skin Syndrome, and its clearance now enables the first company-sponsored formal clinical study for the disease to be conducted. PSS is the second IND cleared indication for QRX003, in addition to Netherton Syndrome. In an ongoing investigator-led pediatric study, subject achieved clinically meaningful improvements by 12 weeks across key objective severity endpoints Modified Ichthyosis Area Severity Index (M-IASI), Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) and a pediatric dermatology-specific quality-of-life measure (CDLQI). Treatment is ongoing and after continued dosing with QRX003 for over 15 months, no adverse events have been reported. FDA expressed no safety concerns regarding study design and duration of dosing. Quoin submitted the IND on June 2, 2026, and received FDA clearance in July 2026. Phase 2 Study Design The Phase 2 study is expected to recruit 6-8 pediatric and adult patients with PSS in both the United States and Europe. In the Phase 2 study, QRX003 will be applied twice-daily to greater than 80% of the patients’ body surface area (BSA) over a 52-week period. The Company is targeting the approval of QRX003 as a potential treatment for PSS in 2028. "For families living with Peeling Skin Syndrome, there is still no approved treatment and no other active clinical development of a potential treatment for the disease. This is what makes FDA clearance to initiate our Phase 2 study so meaningful for this community," said Dr. Michael Myers, CEO of Quoin Pharmaceuticals. "We are excited to start this Phase 2 study of QRX003 and take yet another step toward developing a treatment for another disease that has long been overlooked. This is now the second rare dermatologic indication for QRX003, and it fully reflects Quoin’s mission to provide hope to patient communities and families where none has previously existed. We are particularly encouraged by the FDA expressing no safety concerns in terms of study design and dosing duration which we believe is a very positive indicator as we seek to reach alignment with the agency for our upcoming Phase 3 study in Netherton Syndrome." About Peeling Skin Syndrome (PSS) Generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome (PSS) is a rare autosomal recessive genodermatosis caused by loss-of-function disease-causing variants of the corneodesmosin gene (CDSN), resulting in excessive shedding of the superficial layers of the epidermis. Patients generally suffer from a variety of conditions including severe pain and chronic pruritus (itch). There is currently no approved treatment for PSS. About QRX003 QRX003 is an investigational topical serine protease inhibitor lotion in late-stage development for Netherton Syndrome and other orphan skin diseases. QRX003 has been granted Orphan Drug, Rare Pediatric Disease, and Fast Track designations by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and Orphan Drug Designation in the European Union and Japan for Netherton Syndrome. QRX003 lotion (4%) is currently being evaluated in Phase 2 whole-body clinical trials in patients with Netherton Syndrome. Quoin’s pivotal Phase 3 study is expected to initiate in the second half of 2026, with a potential NDA filing in 2027. QRX003 is also being evaluated for the treatment of Peeling Skin Syndrome. About Quoin Pharmaceuticals Ltd. Quoin Pharmaceuticals Ltd. is a late clinical-stage specialty pharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapeutic products that treat rare and orphan diseases. We are committed to addressing unmet medical needs for patients, their families, communities, and care teams. Quoin's innovative pipeline is focused on two key platform products, QRX003 and QRX009, that collectively have the potential to target a broad number of rare and orphan indications, including Netherton Syndrome, Peeling Skin Syndrome, Palmoplantar Keratoderma, Pachyonychia Congenita, Gorlin Syndrome and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex, Microcystic Lymphatic Malformations, Venous Malformations, Angiofibromas and others.
